The file is named for Visual Studio 2017, but its banner and VisualStudioVersion/MinimumVisualStudioVersion metadata are the Visual Studio 2015-era values (14.0 and 10.0.40219.1), leaving the intended IDE contract unclear.
The file is named for Visual Studio 2022 and declares VisualStudioVersion 17.0, but its banner still says “Visual Studio Version 16”, leaving the solution metadata internally inconsistent.
The version-check fallback tests whether _cur_minor is empty but then assigns _cur_major=0, so a current version lacking a minor component can have its major component incorrectly reset.

LIBTOOL_M4 is hard-coded to misc/libtool.m4 even though this shard’s generated autotools include is m4/libtool.m4, so the libtool-failure recovery path may silently lack its intended project macro file.
The default CONFIG_GUESS_URL uses plain HTTP for downloading build tooling, so the script has no transport-integrity guarantee for that downloaded file.

The Makefile.am existence checks construct dirname from "$CONFIGURE/Makefile.am" rather than the configure template’s containing directory, so they do not reliably test the top-level Makefile.am location.
The download command and destination move leave the URL/auxiliary-directory expansion partly unquoted, making paths or values containing shell-significant whitespace fragile.
The second aclocal invocation after libtoolize records its exit status but never checks it before continuing to autoconf, so a failed regenerated macro scan can be masked.

The dispatcher recognizes VS2010/2012/2015/2017 but has no VS2008 label and no VS2019/VS2022 cases, so an unsupported or newer version falls through to the VS2008 toolchain while the repository contains newer solution files.
The batch file dereferences positional arguments without presence checks and constructs the solution path with a forward slash, leaving invocation and path-format contracts implicit and fragile.
The script recreates dist\win32 and dist\x64 only when those directories already exist, so its apparent clean-directory postcondition is not met on a fresh checkout.

The script interactively generates the default RSA key path and then copies it using CLUSTER_HOSTNAME without validating either operation; absent/failed commands can still be followed by the unconditional success messages.
The remote target is assembled from an unquoted environment variable, so whitespace or shell-significant hostname content is not handled robustly.
The installation pipeline has no failure checks or `set -e`, so failed cleanup, autotools generation, configure, compilation, or installation can be followed by later publication steps.

The script changes to absolute `/config/` and then references `./teamcity-env.sh`, making the final module-generation step depend on an external directory rather than the checked-out config directory.
The generated module file is made mode 777, granting unnecessary write/execute permissions to all users.

The build, install, archive, and directory transitions have no failure checks or `set -e`, allowing a failed build or missing install directory to proceed to artifact publication.

Only VS2010 is explicitly recognized; VS2012 and later inputs fall through to the VS2008 path despite the repository containing newer solution files.
The command uses `%devenv_path%\devenv.exe` even though devenv_path itself contains surrounding quotes, producing a questionable quoted executable path and leaving the intended invocation unclear.
The test-project build and xbeach build are issued back-to-back and only the final command’s status is checked, so failure of the first build can be masked before tests run.
The test executable path is unquoted, so a solution directory containing whitespace cannot be executed reliably.

The script assumes it starts in a directory whose parent contains `trunk/`; it does not anchor paths to the script location or check either `cd`, so invocation from another directory changes the build target.
The unconditional recursive copy of the prior installation has no existence check or failure handling, and with no `set -e` a missing prior installation does not stop the publication pipeline.
Cleanup, generation, configure, build, install, and artifact creation have no failure checks or `set -e`, so stale or partial artifacts can be published after an earlier failure.
The configure invocation places curl library/include flags in FCFLAGS, including a `bin` directory as an include path, leaving the Fortran/compiler flag contract suspicious and toolchain-dependent.
The script assumes its current directory is the installation parent and does not check `chmod`, `cd`, or `scp`, so a missing install tree or transfer failure can be reported as success.
The distribution destination is hard-coded to the gcc 7.3.0/OpenMPI 1.8.3 naming scheme, which conflicts with the newer toolchain naming used by the adjacent TeamCity build script.
The SSH key, source arguments, hostname, and destination are assembled from unquoted expansions, leaving whitespace and shell-significant values unsupported.
The AC_SUBST call has an unusual unmatched-looking quote/bracket sequence (`['$(top_srcdir)/makedepo.py])'`), leaving the generated MAKEDEPO value and macro parsing contract unclear.
The file contains `SUBDIRS=man` but has no terminating newline, so its physical content is nonempty while `wc -l` reports zero lines.

The batch file relies on being launched from its own `bin` directory and does not check doxygen’s exit status before opening the generated index, so a failed generation can be presented as if documentation were ready.

OUTPUT_DIRECTORY and INPUT are relative paths whose base is the directory from which doxygen is started, so using this config outside the companion bin-directory launch context silently changes or breaks the source/output locations.
EXCLUDE is set to the bare relative name `variables.f90` while the INPUT directory is elsewhere; under the documented doxygen path rules this may not exclude the intended source file.
EXTRACT_ALL=YES causes doxygen to disable undocumented-member warnings, so WARN_IF_UNDOCUMENTED=YES does not provide the warning behavior its setting suggests.
The file is entirely blank while the parent doc Makefile.am declares `man` as a subdirectory, leaving the intended man-page build/install contract undefined.

Every formatter output is moved over the original source immediately, with no per-command error check or rollback, so a missing findent executable or failed formatting step can leave the source set partially transformed or replaced.
All source paths are hard-coded relative paths and the batch file does not establish its own directory, so execution from any other working directory targets the wrong locations.
The test runner repeats the program while `ftnunit.lst` exists without a timeout, iteration limit, or exit-status check, so a stale list file or non-terminating test can loop indefinitely.
The invoked test program’s exit status is never checked and output files are overwritten on each iteration, leaving pass/fail and diagnostic retention contracts unclear.
